description: Executable evidence that revoking consent immediately invalidates the cached private contact discovery result, the invite capability gate and the PSI index, and that the revocation itself stays indistinguishable from never having matched.

decision_points.requirement: A cached private contact discovery result stops returning the peer as soon as consent is revoked.
The next invite submission fails its precondition and re-evaluates the capability gate instead of trusting the cached decision.
A revoke with scope any invalidates every scope cache.
The next PSI rotation excludes the peer.
The requester cannot separate a revoked peer from a peer that never matched.

cases.name: directory_lookup_stops_returning_the_peer
cases.given: a private contact discovery result for the peer was cached while consent was active
cases.action: the subject revokes consent, then the same directory lookup runs again
cases.observed: the directory lookup response before and after the revoke
assertions: the cached discovery entry is invalidated by the revoke itself, not by its own expiry
the post-revoke response is the same shape the requester would get for a peer that never matched
no cached entry can be replayed to re-derive the peer

cases.name: cached_invite_gate_is_reevaluated_before_the_next_submission
cases.given: the invite capability gate for this subject evaluated to allowed and was cached
cases.action: revoke consent, then submit the next invite
cases.observed: the authorization decision recorded for the submission
assertions: the submission fails its precondition instead of being admitted from the cached decision
the gate is re-evaluated against current consent state, so a stale cache entry never authorizes the action
consent_revoked is the recorded authorization outcome

cases.name: an_any_scope_revoke_clears_every_scope_cache
cases.given: three separate scopes hold cached decisions derived from the same consent
cases.observed: each scope cache after the revoke
assertions: every scope cache is invalidated, not only the scope named in the most recent grant
a per-scope revoke MUST NOT be substituted for the any-scope semantics
no scope retains an entry that would authorize after the revoke

cases.name: the_next_psi_rotation_excludes_the_peer
cases.given: the PSI index built before the revoke still contains the peer
cases.observed: the membership of the rotated PSI index
assertions: the rotated index excludes the peer
exclusion happens at the rotation boundary and is not deferred to a later one
the pre-rotation index is not queryable as a fallback once the rotation completes

cases.name: revocation_is_not_distinguishable_from_never_matching
cases.given: one peer revoked consent and another never granted it
cases.action: run the same lookup for both
cases.observed: the external response shape and timing for both peers
assertions: both return the same external shape
consent_revoked is an internal authorization outcome and MUST NOT be the reason the requester sees
timing does not separate the two
